subject: aspirin
correct: Resolved suspected TIA: aspirin 300 mg immediately unless contraindicated (bleeding disorder, anticoagulant); no brain imaging needed first (NICE NG128). Ongoing deficit = stroke pathway, no aspirin before imaging.

fixes.old: Give aspirin 300mg now (if haemorrhage unlikely clinically and no CT available).
fixes.new: Give aspirin 300mg now unless contraindicated (NICE NG128: no brain imaging needed first for resolved suspected TIA; anticoagulated or bleeding disorder → specialist advice).

fixes.old: Do NOT give aspirin without excluding haemorrhage if clinically uncertain.
fixes.new: Do NOT give aspirin if symptoms are ongoing (stroke pathway: imaging first), or if anticoagulated or with a bleeding disorder, without specialist advice.

note: The qualifier 'if haemorrhage unlikely clinically and no CT available' and 'do not give without excluding haemorrhage if uncertain' implies imaging gating for resolved TIA, contradicting NG128 and ~40 other statements on the site (including elsewhere on the same page). Risk: GP withholds the loading dose.

subject: platelets
correct: Routine platelet-count monitoring is not required in obstetric patients receiving LMWH only (BSH HIT guideline, Watson et al 2012; RCOG GTG37a). Monitor only if UFH was given first or per specialist plan.

fixes.old: Platelet count at baseline and monthly on LMWH.
fixes.new: Routine platelet monitoring is not needed on LMWH alone in pregnancy (BSH/RCOG); follow the specialist monitoring plan.

note: Pregnancy item. Monthly platelet counts on LMWH alone are not UK guidance and push unnecessary monitoring into primary care.

subject: aspirin
group: APS pregnancy — when to stop aspirin
correct: No single UK national stop date. NICE NG133 (pre-eclampsia) says aspirin until birth; for APS, RCOG GTG17 / local obstetric-haematology protocols vary (stop at about 34–36 weeks or continue to delivery).
note: tools/algorithms/vaginal-bleeding-pregnancy.html states flatly 'Stop aspirin at 36 weeks (haemorrhage risk at delivery).' Everywhere else the site says aspirin 75–150 mg 'from 12 weeks until birth' (NG133). Owner: replace with 'Stop timing per the obstetric/haematology plan (local protocols vary, commonly about 36 weeks; NICE NG133 continues aspirin until birth for pre-eclampsia risk)'? Suggested old string: 'Stop aspirin at 36 weeks (haemorrhage risk at delivery).'

subject: platelets
group: Liver disease — platelet threshold for portal hypertension
correct: Baveno VII: in compensated advanced chronic liver disease, platelets ≤150 × 10⁹/L (or LSM ≥20 kPa) means variceal screening is needed; LSM <15 kPa with platelets ≥150 rules out CSPH. <100 is too low a trigger.

fixes.old: Platelets <100 × 10⁹/L = portal hypertension indicator → hepatology referral plus OGD for varices
fixes.new: Platelets ≤150 × 10⁹/L in suspected advanced liver disease = possible portal hypertension → hepatology referral; variceal screening (OGD) if platelets ≤150 or liver stiffness ≥20 kPa (Baveno VII)

note: The <100 cut-off under-triggers referral and screening for varices. Low clinical-severity error, but the threshold is wrong.
